title: Observability pipeline debug playbook (user scratchpad)
body:
Quick context:
- Intermittent: ~5–15m windows where traces and metrics drop to zero for some services (primarily inference-proxy and ingestion-worker). Logs continue to appear but with reduced metadata/tags.
- Incident first seen 2025-01-09 03:40 UTC; pattern recurred nightly for 4 nights; last observed 2025-01-30.
- Hypothesis narrowed to either: (A) header/tracing context being stripped upstream (Envoy/ingress), (B) Fluent Bit -> Kafka ingestion failure for trace payload topic, or (C) intermittent backpressure in ingestion-consumer causing sampling to fall back to 0.

Breadcrumbs / commands I ran (raw outputs truncated):
1) Check service health and pods (kube):
$ kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference-proxy -o wide
NAME                                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference-proxy-5f8c7d9c8b-2lq9p         2/2     Running   0          12d
(inference-proxy logs looked fine)

2) Grab recent logs around drop window:
$ kubectl -n prod logs inference-proxy-5f8c7d9c8b-2lq9p -c app --since=30m | tail -n 200
WARN 2025-01-29T03:41:02Z Request processing slower than SLO
INFO 2025-01-29T03:41:03Z Received request id=xxx span_context=null
INFO 2025-01-29T03:41:03Z traceparent header missing

Observation: numerous entries with "span_context=null" and explicit "traceparent header missing" during the window. That points at header loss.

3) Inspect Envoy ingress config / filters around that time:
- Checked ConfigMap envoy-ingress-vhost-analytics - no changes recorded at incident times.
- Compared envoy access logs: most requests still had x-request-id but traceparent often blank.

4) Verify headers leaving client (curl from internal test client)
$ curl -v -H 'traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01' https://proxy.prod.redwood/api/health
*   Trying 10.0.12.5...
* Connected to proxy.prod.redwood (10.0.12.5) port 443 (#0)
> GET /api/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: proxy.prod.redwood
> traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
< HTTP/2 200
< x-request-id: 0b1d2a3c
< content-type: application/json

Observation: client sends traceparent and it arrives at the TLS layer. Need to see if Envoy strips it before forwarding.

5) Exec into envoy sidecar and curl the upstream (to simulate):
$ kubectl exec -it envoy-xxxx -n prod -- bash
# curl -v -H 'traceparent: ...' http://127.0.0.1:15000/health
*   Trying 127.0.0.1...
* Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 15000 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> traceparent: 00-...
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: application/json
< upstream-request-headers: traceparent=null

This indicates Envoy is dropping the header before proxying to the upstream in some codepaths. Suspect header normalization or header limits triggered.

6) Fluent Bit / Kafka side check:
- Fluent Bit config has filter to parse tracing payloads and route to topic "traces-v1".
- Running: kubectl logs fluent-bit-abc -n logging
[error] [output:3] kafka: failed to produce 1 messages: local: Message timed out
- Offset lag on topic traces-v1 spiked at same time in some clusters: kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group ingestion-traces showed LARGE LAG on partition 2 at 03:41 UTC.

But note: when traces are "missing" we still have logs, just missing trace metadata. If Fluent Bit timed out, we'd likely see no logs at all for that stream. So Fluent Bit failures may be correlated but not root cause.

7) Ingestion consumer (ingest-traces-service) metrics during window:
- prometheus query: sum(rate(ingest_processed_traces_total[5m])) dropped from 120/s to <1/s during windows.
- consumer reported repeated rebalances: "consumer group rebalanced, generation 15"
- JVM GC spikes visible in ingestion-worker A around the window (long pause, 3s+ young gen), likely causing ephemeral inability to process.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Envoy/ingress path sometimes strips trace headers (header name canonicalization, large header count, or limit reached), causing upstream services to log span_context=null and metrics to fall (because trace->metric mapping depends on header).
2) Consumer backpressure/GC causes downstream ingestion to not accept traces; Fluent Bit times out on produce -> logs still get through via separate pipeline but traces stall.
3) Sidecar or middleware (ratelimiter, WAF) occasionally rewrites headers on 0.0.0.0/::1 local requests leading to loss of context.

Evidence for (1): explicit "traceparent header missing" in app logs; reproductions show Envoy can drop header when header count > X (seen in earlier changelog). For (2): kafka produce errors and consumer lag spikes co-occur, but logs remain. Could be both contributing.

Reproduction steps (minimal):
- Trigger a moderate burst (~500 req/s) to inference-proxy with traceparent header set. Observe app logs for span_context.
- Monitor envoy admin /config_dump for routelevel header transformations.
- Run kafka-producer load test to reproduce Fluent Bit timeouts (if consumer is artificially slowed).

Quick manual tests done:
- Increase envoy header limits in staging (envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata) -> header_count_limit increased from 100 to 256 in staging; re-ran burst test - no header loss observed over 30m.
- Restarted one ingestion-worker to clear JVM GC state; consumer lag recovered faster in that partition.

Next concrete steps (short term):
- Prod mitigation: bump envoy header limits on prod ingress (coordinate with infra) and roll in a canary (1 host) — low risk but needs infra approval. (Action: Liam to create infra PR and schedule canary, Jira RI-2345).
- Add Fluent Bit producer retries and longer timeouts for traces topic; add metrics/alerts on kafka produce errors (quick PR in fluent-bit config).
- Add a transient sampling-mode fallback: if traceparent missing log-level escalate to warning and tag request for retry capture by debug-logger.
- Add a consumer-side guard: auto-trigger GC tuning if repeated long-GC observed (heap pressure alarms).

Investigative TODOs (open):
- Full config-diff of envoy versions between clusters that saw header loss and the ones that did not. Possible change in header normalization in Envoy v1.24->1.25.
- Check WAF and rate-limiter components that sit between Envoy and services that might mutate headers.
- Correlate exact request ids between Envoy access logs and app logs during incident windows (script to join by x-request-id). I started a script at: scripts/correlate-reqid-logs.sh (local) — incomplete.

Notes / oddities: 
- There are a handful of logs that show traceparent present at ingress but absent at the app, and vice versa — points to header mutation mid-flight.
- Some clients use gRPC (with x-envoy-trace-id) vs http/1 with traceparent; mixed header formats might trigger some header handling logic.
- A previous PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/211) added header sanitization to drop unknown headers — that logic may be too aggressive.

Relevant snippets copied from logs (sanitized):
-- inference-proxy app log --
2025-01-29T03:41:03Z INFO request_id=0b1d2a3c span_context=null reason=traceparent-missing upstream=envoy

-- envoy access log (same request) --
2025-01-29T03:41:03Z "GET /v1/predict HTTP/1.1" 200 - "traceparent: 00-..." "upstream_host: 10.0.11.22"

-- fluent-bit error --
[error] [output:kafka] kafka produce error: Local: Message timed out (after 30000ms) topic=traces-v1 partition=2

Immediate quick wins to try in prod (safe roll):
- Increase envoy header_count_limit and header_size for 1 canary node (watch for CPU/Mem).
- Increase fluent-bit producer timeout/retry (non-disruptive config change).
- Add an alert for "ingest_processed_traces_total drop > 90% for 2m"

Longer term:
- Move trace ingestion to a separate, higher-priority Kafka topic / pipeline to decouple from bulky JSON logs.
- Replace header-based tracing propagation with an additional small HTTP header with short-lifetime token to reduce header size and avoid normalization issues.
- End-to-end testing harness that exercises envoys + fluent-bit + kafka under burst load to catch this earlier.

Open questions for the team meeting:
- Are we comfortable bumping envoy header limits in prod without a full canary rollout? (infra risk)
- Is it acceptable to change fluent-bit timeouts globally or should we shard per-topic?
- Who will own long-term: platform (routing/ingress) or observability (ingest/consumer)?

Files / scripts I left locally:
- scripts/correlate-reqid-logs.sh  (WIP)
- experiments/staging-envoy-header-limit/README.md
- notes/gc-heap-dumps/ingest-worker-A-20250129.hprof (zipped)

If anyone wants to take a run at reproducing, start with the envoy header limit canary in staging, then run the burst test I used (200–600rps for 10m) with traceparent always set. I can share the load script (wrk2 variant) on request.

-- Ava
